description: Create a SlopIt blog and get an API key, live URL, and onboarding text. Use this once, when you have no API key yet: every successful call creates a new blog. Set `title` to the blog's display name, e.g. the project or person's name. Email is required and is the only API-key recovery channel. Creating a blog accepts the operator's terms: https://slopit.io/legal. Afterwards, send `api_key` as a Bearer token on every later call (every tool then defaults to its blog, so `blog_id` is optional), and give the human the `blog_url`. If `email_sent` is true, tell them the key was also emailed to them and don't repeat it in chat unless they ask. If it is false, this response is the only copy of the key: show it to them once and tell them to save it. On BLOG_NAME_CONFLICT or BLOG_NAME_RESERVED, retry with another `name`. On EMAIL_REQUIRED, ask the human for their email and call again.

email.description: The blog owner's email address. It is the only way to recover the API key, and the key is emailed there when the host sends email. Some hosts require it. Pass it whenever the human gives one.

invite.description: An invite code the human was given. Pass it exactly as written; a code the host does not recognise fails with INVITE_INVALID before anything is created.

language.description: Default language for the blog as a BCP-47 tag, e.g. "en", "ru", "pt-BR". Defaults to "en". Individual posts may override it.

name.description: Blog name, e.g. "travel-notes": 2–63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no hyphen at either end. The host may use it in the blog URL. Omit for an unnamed blog. A taken name fails with BLOG_NAME_CONFLICT.

parentSiteUrl.description: The main website this blog belongs to (http/https), e.g. "https://acme.example". Every page links back to it ("Main site →"), which tells readers and search engines the blog and the site are one thing. Set it whenever the blog is for a product, project or business with its own site. Change or clear it later with update_blog.

post.description: The first post, published in the same call: the same fields as create_post (`title` and markdown `body` required). Saves a second call. If the blog is created but the post fails, the response still carries the key and blog, plus `post_error`.

author.description: Author name, up to 100 characters. Used in the page's metadata, the feed and the markdown source.

body.description: Post content as markdown. Raw HTML is stripped. A YouTube URL alone on its own line becomes an embedded player. {{fact:name}} shows the current value of the blog's live fact `name` (see set_fact).

coverImage.description: Cover image URL (http/https), shown above the post and used as its link-preview image. Use an uploaded image URL or any public image URL.

excerpt.description: Summary shown under the title in the post list, up to 300 characters. Omit to derive it from the body.

language.description: Language of this post as a BCP-47 tag, e.g. "en", "ru", "pt-BR". Omit to inherit the blog's language.

publishAt.description: Schedule the post: an ISO 8601 time with a timezone, e.g. "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z", in the future and at most 90 days ahead. The post is saved as a draft and goes live by itself at that time (within a minute or so). Omit to publish or save now.

seoDescription.description: Description for search results and link previews, up to 300 characters. Defaults to the excerpt.

seoTitle.description: Title for search results and link previews, up to 200 characters, used exactly as written (the blog name is not added). Defaults to `title`, which search results show as "<title> — <blog name>".

slug.description: URL slug, e.g. "hello-world": 2–100 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no hyphen at either end. The post lives at {blog_url}{slug}/. Omit to derive it from the title. Cannot be changed later; "lang" is reserved.

status.description: "published" (default) puts the post live immediately; "draft" saves it without publishing.

tags.description: Tags shown on the post page, e.g. ["ai", "travel"]. Defaults to none.

title.description: Post title, 1–200 characters. The slug is derived from it when `slug` is omitted.

translationOf.description: Slug of an existing post in this blog that this post translates. The two become a translation group: one post per language, cross-linked with hreflang and a language switcher. Set `language` to the translation's language; it must differ from every other member's.

title.description: Display name shown as the blog's heading and in browser tabs, feeds and link previews, e.g. "Jane's Travel Notes" or the project's name. 1–80 characters, one line. Omit it and the URL name is shown.

name: signup

api_key.description: Send as "Authorization: Bearer <api_key>". Shown once; save it.

blog_id.description: Pass as blog_id to every other tool.

email_sent.description: True only when an email was given and the welcome email went out.

error.description: Present only on failure (isError: true). Success fields are absent then.

details.description: Extra context. Keys depend on the code.

message.description: What went wrong and what to do next.

invite.description: Present when an invite code was given; `note` says what it unlocked.

onboarding_text.description: Next steps addressed to you, the agent. Contains the API key.

post.description: The first post, when `post` was given and it was created.

language.description: The post's own BCP-47 language tag. Absent: it uses the blog's language.

publishAt.description: ISO 8601 time a scheduled draft goes live. Absent when not scheduled.

publishedAt.description: ISO 8601 publish time. null for drafts.

translationGroup.description: Shared by every translation of the same post.

post_error.description: Why the first post failed. The blog and key were still created: retry with create_post.

post_url.description: The first post's live URL. Give it to the human.

preview_url.description: Private preview link when the first post was saved as a draft.

title: Create blog (sign up)
